chunks: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Yunus ibn Ya'qub from Mu'ttab who said:
Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) used to command us: 'When the fruit ripens, we should take it out and sell it, and buy back with the Muslims day for day.'

key_terms.أَدْرَكَتِ الثَّمَرَةُ: The fruit ripened or reached maturity
key_terms.الْحُكْرَةِ: Hoarding (implied by the chapter title context)
key_terms.يَوْمًا بِيَوْمٍ: Day for day (a specific mode of trade)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling and repurchasing fruit day for day in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on *Hukrah* (hoarding), this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) prescribes a specific mechanism to prevent market manipulation by ensuring immediate sale and quick repurchase. This 'day for day' transaction serves to maintain liquidity and prevent artificial scarcity of essential agricultural goods, reflecting the Shia emphasis on fair trade practices and social economic justice.
